notes: Mikazuki style-test assets (locked 3 Oct 2026). Pixel art: render with nearest-neighbour and whole-number zoom only.

grass.animatedNote: Only tall-grass and flower tiles sway; plain grass stays still. Draw the -sway sheet in place of the still tile and start each tile at frame (col+row) % 4 so a soft wind wave rolls across the meadow.

litter.note: darker grass with fallen leaves; used where maps/town.json groundStyle says "litter" (under thick groves)

mixes.rule: each grass tile uses the mix named by maps/town.json groundStyle ("" = default); pick the category by weight, then a file at random (seeded)

overlays.rule: draw tile-water, then for every land neighbour draw the matching overlay on top. Edges use the 4 side neighbours; a corner overlay only when that diagonal is land and both sides next to it are water.

water.variantNote: 4 variants x 4 frames (128x16 sheets, 32x16 frames). Pick a variant per tile at random (seeded) so the river does not show a grid; all tiles share one frame clock so the ripples flow together. Ripples stay inside the diamond, so any variants can sit side by side.

slums.note: The Slums' ground (maps/slums.json). ground: floor tiles per kind, 32x16, anchor = diamond centre; pick a variant per tile, seeded by col,row. canal: a 4-frame strip on a shared clock, banks from tiles.water's overlays. Raised ground (tiles/slums/slums-elevation-README.md): one level = 16 px; cliffs, rim, cap and ramps are 32x32 pieces anchored on the diamond centre of the tile they stand on (16,24). cliffs: <material>.l / .r = the wall shown when the SW / SE neighbour is lower (one per level of drop, 16 px apart), variant seeded by col,row. rim nw/ne: outline on a raised top whose NW / NE neighbour is lower. cap w/e: corner edges. ramps: <surface>.<dir> = [part 1 (low cell), part 2], dir = the way you walk up.

jackpot-booth.collision: block the centre tile and the 4 tiles beside it (a plus shape); the 4 corner tiles of the base stay walkable
jackpot-booth.note: tall version (3 Oct), redrawn to human scale

twigos-house.interaction: the door is on the SE gable end. If the house's top (back) tile is (col,row), the tile in front of the door is (col+3,row+1); stepping onto it returns the player to twigo's room
twigos-house.note: tall version (3 Oct): 42 px walls, door about head height

notice-board.collision: block the 2 tiles under the posts (the back row of the 2x2)
notice-board.interaction: stand in front and press to open notices; text comes from the game, not the sprite

leaderboard-monument.interaction: show the top-3 names as game text on the gold plaque area or in a popup

sari-sari-store.interaction: door on the SE face: the tile in front is (col+3,row+1) from the top tile; opens the sari-sari store (what /redeem sells)

parlor.interaction: door on the SE face (a gap in the railing): the tile in front is (col+3,row+1) from the top tile; opens the Parlor (change your look and the title you show)
parlor.note: added 6 Oct; same footprint as the sari-sari store; the blank sign has no text

bank.interaction: door at the top of the steps on the SW face: the tile in front is (col+1,row+3); opens the bank

tanod-outpost.collision: block all 4x3 (4 tiles along the right edge, 3 along the left)
tanod-outpost.interaction: door on the SW face, left side: the tile in front is (col+0,row+3); the blank white sign is for game text like TANOD; jailed players stand by the barred windows with fx-jail-bars

casino.interaction: entrance under the canopy on the SW face: the tile in front is (col+1..2,row+4); the blank neon marquee is for game text

mine-entrance.interaction: tunnel mouth on the SW face: the tile in front is (col+1,row+3)

arena.collision: block the outer ring of the 6x6; the sand floor inside can be walkable for fights
arena.interaction: gate on the SW face wall: the tile in front is (col+2..3,row+6)

layers.rule: same canvas and anchor as the full image. Draw "back" (stands, inner walls, sand floor) at the depth of the footprint top corner so everyone on the sand is in front of it; draw "front" (the two front walls, front tower, base plinth) at the normal front-corner depth so players on the sand go behind its rim. back + front together equal building-arena.png exactly.

characters.anchorMeaning: feet: bottom row, between columns 15 and 16
characters.mirroring: w, sw, nw are already baked as mirrors of e, se, ne (files exist for all 8)

idle.note: breathing 0,1,2,3,2,1 with a blink at the top

sit.note: seated hold with a 1 px breath; diagonals only, for benches. Play it directly (no sit-down transition); stand up by switching to idle

wave.note: plays once (0.8 s), then back to idle. E is the same art as SE, W the same as SW

cheer.note: happy hop with arms up; play once alongside an emote icon, then back to idle. E is the same art as SE, W the same as SW. The feet leave the ground during the hop, but the cell anchor stays fixed

face.note: no face layer for n, ne, nw (back views)

characters.sheetLayout: frames left to right in one row, 32x48 each; every layer matches the body sheet exactly (zero offset)

colourKeys.comment: grey key ramps, palette-swapped at runtime (light to dark)

wardrobe.keys: MAIN ramp (DCDCF0,A8A8C8,74749A,48486A) = the item's main colour; TRIM ramp (F0E0C8,C0A888,8A7258) = its accent (stripes, jacket inner shirt, polo collar, cargo pockets, all shoe colours); FBEEE9 = sneaker sole (never swapped)
wardrobe.glassesNote: glasses layers exist for s, se, e, sw, w (all anims with a face). Back views (n, ne, nw) draw no glasses. Frame colour is on the MAIN ramp (48486A/74749A), so it can be recoloured
wardrobe.hairNote: All 8 dirs, all anims (rot, walk, idle, sit, wave, cheer). Hair ramp keys E8E8E8,B4B4B4,7C7C7C,4A4A4A; navy outline 1E1B3A. long and ponytail already sit behind the body below the neck in side views. mohawk leaves the sides bald by design.
wardrobe.hatNote: Hats are recoloured on the MAIN ramp (DCDCF0,A8A8C8,74749A,48486A). beanie and cap ship a clip mask per frame: white pixels = hide the hair layer there (erase hair under the hat) before drawing the hat. ribbon has no clip mask and hides no hair. When a clipping hat is worn with 'buns', draw 'crop' instead (hatHairFallback).

colourPresets.note: swap MAIN (4 colours) with any preset; for TRIM use its first 3 colours

skinTones.keys: swap the 4 skin keys on the body AND face layers (the mouth uses a skin key on purpose)

faceTweak.note: darken brows and lashes on the deep tone so they stay readable

classes.note: The six classes (data: classes/classes.json). Combat poses per class and anim: for each direction the body, the face (s/se/e/sw/w) and the weapon layers behind (back, drawn before the body) and in front (front, after the body, face and clothes), in draw order. Weapon cells are 64x64 with the 32x48 body cell at bodyOffset (Slingshot's weapon is 32x48 like the body). Every direction has its own files: nothing is mirrored. rest: the town resting weapon over the base idle and walk (same frame index as the body), or for the Hilot the balm-float loop on its own clock. launch: fx spawn points per anim/dir/frame in 64-cell coords (launch.json), or for the Slingshot the README's release-frame points in body-cell coords.

launchPoints.note: pebble launch on the release frame, body-cell px (README)

npcs.anchorMeaning: feet, as the players' (so they depth-sort like players)

wave.note: plays once, then back to idle

cheer.note: plays once, then back to idle

whistle.note: the Tanod only; plays once, then back to idle

sit.note: seated on the ground catching her breath (the Mosang race's arthritis and asthma stops)

fall.note: trips and goes down; plays once and holds its last frame (the Mosang race's falls)

getup.note: back up from the fall's last frame; ends on idle frame 0

portrait.note: frame 0 eyes open, frame 1 a blink

npcs.rule: flat pre-baked sheets (never through the paper-doll compositor): one row of cell-sized frames per animation and direction, all 8 directions drawn (no mirroring); name, title and lines come from the dialogue file

quests.note: Quests (quests/quests.json: main and side, their objectives and the givers' lines). Main quests are violet and side quests yellow everywhere a quest shows (tracker, log, toast, the marker over the giver): the palette's nearest to #9D7BFF and #F2C94C.

fence.rule: fence-nw sits on the tile's top-left edge, fence-ne on its top-right edge (both back edges, so draw before characters on that tile). To fence a front edge, use the neighbour tile's back edge. Cap the open end of a run with fence-post on the next tile along. Block movement across the fenced edge, not the tile.
fence.use: optional world prop: place it anywhere to frame yards, gardens or the town edge; nothing depends on it yet

jnpHands.note: jack en poy hands: 0 bato, 1 papel, 2 gunting; points right, the sleeve runs off the left edge (flip X for the opponent). Skin keys + cloth-main keys (cuff), recoloured per player like the paper doll

vs.note: the arena's VS: frame 0 plain, 1-3 a glint sweep played once, then back to 0

vsSpeedlines.note: speed lines on transparent (the arena's VS screen, on white): one tile squished to the VS band's height (thick lines top and bottom), a whole-number scale sideways; tiles and scrolls sideways

arenaViewers.note: arena spectators: ten front-facing cheering loops (9 frames); the stands and the front row of the arena screen

arenaModes.note: the arena menu's icons: 0 Vs Bot, 1 Vs Player

questIcon.note: the quest button's scroll (32x32, cut down from the 48x48 art in mikazuki-assets by dropping its least distinct rows and columns)

equipSlots.note: grey silhouettes for empty equipment slots, one 16x16 frame each

skillIcons.note: skill icons on the shared navy rounded-square frame, 32x32 (the hotbar and the Skills panel at 1x). {skill} = the skill's name from classes.json in lower case, words joined by '-' (Quick Shot = quick-shot). have: the icons there are per class; shared: one icon for every class (Dash), used when the class has none of its own. Skills without one show their initials. Every skill has one now.

classIcons.note: round class badges: 32 by default, 16 redrawn for the chat and the avatar, 64 for the class cards

notes_ui: All UI is drawn at 1x and scaled by the same whole-number zoom as the world. Text is never baked in: draw it with Minecraft.ttf.
notes_items: Item art by id (dig items in the bot's dig/items.ts, rewards in games/rewards.ts): icon = 16x16 for small rows, showcase = 32x32 for pop-ups, anim = a 32x32 looping sheet shown instead of the showcase where there is one. Ids without art are simply absent (the game shows the emoji/name). Draw at whole-number scales with nearest-neighbour.

houses.interaction: door on the SE face: the tile in front is (col+3,row+1) from the top tile
houses.note: Players' houses in the neighbourhood (6 Oct): five types (parts.json: layers bottom to top, one slot each), recoloured per slot from swatches.json. Layers are drawn in key colours (parts.json keys): each layer's own family (main, stone or trim, whichever it has most of) takes its slot's swatch (main/stone shade for shade, trim's three onto the swatch's last three), glow takes the windows swatch, leaf/flower the plants swatch, trim in other layers the house's trimSlot swatch; the door knob (#F8BF27) and outlines stay.

equipment.note: Equipment items (items/equipment.json): id, name, slot, who can use it, level, rarity, stats and icons. The training weapons are the first.

mobs.note: Mobs (world/mobs.ts): one sheet per animation and direction, file = pattern with {anim} and {dir}; anchor = the pixel between the feet. Only mobs of active zones load.
